run.brief: Portalo — a game-graphics demo app, designed and built by appbox

screens.label: Splash
screens.summary: Animated logo first paint under 300ms — the brand moment, nothing else
screens.summaryPlain: The opening screen: the Portalo logo animates in fast, nothing else loads here

screens.label: Startup
screens.summary: Loading orchestration — kits warm up behind a real progress line, never a spinner
screens.summaryPlain: The loading screen: demos get ready behind an honest progress bar, not a spinning wheel

screens.label: Sign In
screens.summary: One-tap sign-in — Apple/Google, the session persists; no demo ever asks twice
screens.summaryPlain: Sign in once with Apple or Google — the app remembers you, no demo asks again

screens.label: Demo Dashboard
screens.summary: Every demo one tap away — live status chips show which kits are ready
screens.summaryPlain: The home screen: every demo a tap away, with chips showing what is ready to run

screens.label: Demo Index
screens.summary: The full demo catalog as cards — grouped by kit, filterable by media type
screens.summaryPlain: All demos as cards, grouped by the library they show off — easy to browse

screens.label: Rive Demo
screens.summary: State-machine Rive animation — inputs scrubbed live from the control panel
screens.summaryPlain: An interactive Rive animation — the side panel drives its state machine live

screens.label: Lottie Demo
screens.summary: Lottie playback with frame-accurate scrubbing and loop control
screens.summaryPlain: A Lottie animation you can play, pause and scrub frame by frame

screens.label: dotLottie Demo
screens.summary: Bundled .lottie archives — theme variants switched without a reload
screens.summaryPlain: The packed dotLottie format — swap its baked-in themes without reloading

screens.label: 3D Model Demo
screens.summary: glTF model viewer — orbit, zoom and lighting presets at 60 fps
screens.summaryPlain: Spin and zoom a 3D model with finger gestures — smooth 60 fps

screens.label: 3D Scene Demo
screens.summary: A composed three.js scene — camera dolly, fog and light probes live
screens.summaryPlain: A full 3D scene built with three.js — camera moves, fog and lights adjustable live

screens.label: Mini Game
screens.summary: A playable mini-game — frame budget proven on the real device, HUD from kit primitives
screens.summaryPlain: A small game you can actually play — proof the graphics stay smooth on a real phone

screens.label: Maps Demo
screens.summary: Map tiles with kit credentials — styles and overlays from the maps kit
screens.summaryPlain: A live map — tiles only load with valid credentials, styles come from the maps kit

screens.label: Kit Credentials
screens.summary: API keys per kit, validated on save — a bad key fails loudly, never silently
screens.summaryPlain: Where the API keys live — each one is checked when you save it, so nothing breaks quietly

screens.label: App Config
screens.summary: Runtime flags and demo defaults — editable in-app, persisted across restarts
screens.summaryPlain: The settings screen — switches for how demos behave, remembered between launches

designThread.text: The game HUD feels loud — the score banner shouts. Can it breathe?
Softened — the banner now sits on 12% accent with a hairline border; pause stays solid ink. Checkpoint cp-3 below, one tap reverts.
designThread.textPlain: Made it calmer — the score banner is now a soft tint instead of a loud fill; the pause button stays bold. Saved as cp-3 below, one tap undoes it.

designThread.text: Compact rung: the control bar covers the play field.
Docked — under 600px the bar pins to the viewport edge and the play field pads for it. cp-4.
designThread.textPlain: Fixed — on phone-size screens the control bar pins to the screen edge instead of floating over the play field. Saved as cp-4.
